name: AccessGate
summary: Hides an action the user cannot take, or shows it inert with the reason.

a11y.apg: No role and no box of its own: it renders the child, a replacement, or the child made inert. What it does carry is the accessibility decision. In disable mode it sets aria-disabled and never disabled — measured on 2026-08-13, a disabled control leaves the tab order, so the reason hung on it is never read by anyone using a keyboard, and the span wrapper other libraries document fixes the pointer and not the keyboard. Hiding is the safer default when the action would mean nothing to this user; disabling is right when they should know it exists and why it is closed.

props.name: allowed
props.description: REQUIRED, and it is an ANSWER, not a question: Aurea holds no rules, roles or policies. You decide, from whatever your app uses, and pass the result. THIS IS NOT SECURITY — hiding a button stops nobody from calling the API. The server is what refuses; this only avoids offering what would be refused.

props.name: children
props.description: REQUIRED. A single element — the action being gated. When allowed, it comes through untouched, with no wrapper.

props.name: mode
props.description: hide removes the action from the DOM, which is what @casl/react does and the right default when the action would mean nothing to this user. disable keeps it visible and inert, for when they should know it exists — react-admin is the reference that lets you pick, and the pick is the whole reason this component exists.

props.name: reason
props.description: REQUIRED when mode is disable, and the type enforces it: an action that says "no" without saying why is worse than one that is simply absent. It is shown in a Tooltip on the inert control.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Only in hide mode: what takes the place of the action. Use it for a read-only rendering of the same information, not for a second "you cannot do this" message.
